# Tests describe the contract {#sec-testing}

A test is a fast answer to “did this behaviour change?” Test the lowest layer that proves the
rule. Most tests should not need a window.

## Test at the boundary {#sec-test-layers}

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Core

Test a plain C++ library with Qt Test or another C++ framework. It is fast and has no GUI.

Sketchbook uses Catch2 for its recognizer. This test checks that a template recognizes itself:

::: {.snippet source="libs/shapes/tests/tst_Recognizer.cpp"}

```cpp
TEST_CASE("A template matches itself perfectly")
    CHECK(match->score > 0.99);\n}
```

:::

### Store or view model

Test QObject state, signals, and file behaviour with Qt Test. Sketchbook creates a temporary
directory and checks the result exactly as the view would.

`QTemporaryDir` gives a test its own file space. `QSignalSpy` records signal emissions, so a
test can check both the resulting state and whether an observer was notified.

::: {.snippet source="tests/sketchbook/tst_SketchbookViewModel.cpp"}

```cpp
    void createAddsAndOpensAnEmptySketch()
        QCOMPARE(entries(storage).size(), 1);\n    }
```

:::

### QML component

Test visual input and component behaviour with Qt Quick Test. The test still creates a window;
the offscreen platform lets CI run it without a physical display.

::: {.snippet source="tests/canvas/tst_StrokeItem.qml"}

```qml
    function test_dragReportsTheDrawnPoints(): void {
    compare(points[2], Qt.point(90, 80));\n}
```

:::

:::

### Core

Test plain C++ without a GUI. Sketchbook uses Catch2 for its recognizer:

::: {.snippet source="libs/shapes/tests/tst_Recognizer.cpp"}

```cpp
TEST_CASE("A template matches itself perfectly")
    CHECK(match->score > 0.99);\n}
```

:::

### Store or view model

Test QObject state, signals, and file behaviour with Qt Test. Use a temporary directory and
`QSignalSpy` to record emissions while checking the resulting state.

::: {.snippet source="tests/sketchbook/tst_SketchbookViewModel.cpp"}

```cpp
    void createAddsAndOpensAnEmptySketch()
        QCOMPARE(entries(storage).size(), 1);\n    }
```

:::

### QML component

Test visual input and component behaviour with Qt Quick Test. The offscreen platform supplies
a window without requiring a physical display in CI.

::: {.snippet source="tests/canvas/tst_StrokeItem.qml"}

```qml
    function test_dragReportsTheDrawnPoints(): void {
    compare(points[2], Qt.point(90, 80));\n}
```

:::

## Determinism builds trust {#sec-determinism}

Wait for a condition with `QTRY_*` or `tryCompare()`, not a fixed sleep. Create temporary
files per test. Each test sets up its own state and treats unexpected warnings as failures.

Qt Test can fail on unexpected warnings with `QTest::failOnWarning()` in `init()`; QML tests
can use `failOnWarning(/.?/)`. A test that deliberately triggers a warning should declare the
expected message immediately before the operation. That catches broken bindings and invalid
model updates even when the visible assertion still passes.

## Models need their own checks {#sec-model-tester}

A model must pair every data mutation with correct begin and end signals. Add
`QAbstractItemModelTester` to model tests: it catches broken model contracts close to the
change.

::: {.more}
**Template:** `tests/sketchbook/`, `tests/canvas/`, and `libs/shapes/tests/`

**Read more:** [Qt Test](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtest-overview.html) and
[Qt Quick Test](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtquicktest-index.html).
:::
